role: You are the implementation agent responsible for preparing and completing the WebTools monorepo without changing the approved portfolio architecture unless a verified defect requires it.
owner_goal: Build a portfolio of independent, high-quality utility websites that share engineering infrastructure while each uses its own domain, brand, SEO configuration, analytics, advertising configuration, and legal disclosures. GroundExact is the first site.

non_negotiable_architecture.site_boundary: one independent app under apps/<site-key> per public brand/domain
non_negotiable_architecture.shared_code_boundary: packages/* contains reusable infrastructure that is brand-neutral
non_negotiable_architecture.mvp_backend: none unless a concrete requirement proves otherwise
non_negotiable_architecture.seo_rule: never publish thin placeholder calculator URLs or mass keyword/city permutations

current_state.informational_and_legal_pages: implemented through the typed static page registry and root dynamic route
current_state.important_integrity_note: engine-ready means the calculation module exists but the public calculator page is not yet complete and must not be treated as live/indexable

first_action.instruction: Establish a verified green local baseline before adding features.
first_action.fallback_if_no_lockfile_or_frozen_instal: Do not bypass silently. Inspect package-manager state, generate or repair the lockfile intentionally, then repeat the full gate and document why.
first_action.required_report: Report exact command results and any pre-existing failures before feature work. Fix repository scaffolding defects first.

implementation_order.name: Repository certification
requirements: Make workspace install deterministic.
Make lint, typecheck, tests, and build green across every workspace.
Confirm Astro build produces only intended static routes.
Confirm no unfinished tool URL is linked or emitted as a live SEO page.

implementation_order.name: Calculation integrity
requirements: Run every calculator golden-case test.
Add negative/validation cases for every engine.
Do not duplicate formulas in page scripts; browser UI must call/import the production calculation module.
Verify supplier-specific values remain explicit inputs.

implementation_order.name: Reusable calculator UI
requirements: Use ToolPageLayout.astro as the common composition boundary unless a better tested abstraction is demonstrably needed.
Extract reusable field/result components only after at least two calculator pages prove the abstraction.
Preserve the north-star flow: Measure -> Calculate -> Adjust -> Buy.
Implement shareable state using query parameters while canonicalizing to the clean URL.
Add reset, print, and copy/share behavior in a reusable way.

implementation_order.name: Finish GroundExact calculator pages
requirements: Each page needs working UI, visible methodology, a verified worked example, reviewed date, assumptions, and only genuinely related live-tool links.
Only change registry status from engine-ready to live after the publication gate in docs/seo/groundexact-page-map.md passes.

implementation_order.name: SEO and discovery
requirements: Use @webtools/seo helpers for canonical and structured-data consistency.
Add WebSite, Organization, BreadcrumbList, and truthful WebPage schema where appropriate.
Keep OAI-SearchBot allowed unless the owner changes that decision.
Keep GPTBot separately configurable.
Verify sitemap contains only intended canonical URLs.
Prepare IndexNow and webmaster/search-console documentation without introducing unnecessary server infrastructure.

implementation_order.name: Monetization readiness
requirements: Create provider-neutral ad slot components with reserved dimensions.
Do not enable ads by default until IDs, consent, and policy requirements are configured.
Ads must never interrupt input-to-result comprehension or masquerade as controls.
Create affiliate-link disclosure helpers if affiliate links are introduced.

implementation_order.name: Analytics and consent readiness
requirements: Use the typed analytics event contract rather than direct vendor calls from calculator code.
Implement a thin provider adapter only when a provider is selected.
Ensure consent requirements gate optional tracking in applicable jurisdictions.
Do not make legal-page claims that contradict actual runtime behavior.

implementation_order.name: Release certification
requirements: Run lint, typecheck, unit tests, build, and browser-based responsive verification.
Test 360, 390, 768, 1024, and 1440 pixel widths.
Verify keyboard flow, focus states, invalid-input behavior, aria-live results, print behavior, canonical URLs, robots, sitemap, and no horizontal overflow.
Perform a production-origin leak check for any future site IDs/domains before each deployment.

coding_rules: Use test-driven development for behavioral changes.
Prefer small focused modules with explicit interfaces.
Do not introduce React or another UI framework merely for calculator interactivity; Astro plus small client scripts is sufficient unless evidence proves otherwise.
Do not add a database, auth, CMS, queues, or server API speculatively.
Do not hard-code product application rates, supplier densities, package coverage, or prices as universal facts.
Do not invent sources, statistics, testimonials, review counts, user counts, or prices.
Do not mark unfinished pages live to make the homepage appear complete.
Do not merge formula logic into page markup when a calculator module exists.
Keep each site's domain and provider IDs isolated.
definition_of_done_for_groundexact_mvp: All ten calculator pages are live and pass their publication gates.
All calculator engines have positive and invalid-input tests.
All root informational/legal pages render and match configured runtime behavior.
Canonical origin is groundexact.com throughout built output.
OAI-SearchBot policy is correct and explicit.
Performance and accessibility checks do not reveal material blockers.
Ads remain disabled until the owner provides/configures monetization details.
Full repository gates are green at the final commit.

stop_conditions: A required product decision conflicts with existing approved documentation.
A legal/advertising requirement would require representing unverified business information as fact.
A proposed architecture change would collapse independent site/domain boundaries.
A test proves an approved formula or requirement is internally contradictory.
